summary: This is a sound rewrite stage aimed at the problem's largest gap (full verify_16/32 at 2.2 TB/s, 2.3x floor; DIAGNOSIS action 1). The gate makes it fail-safe. Its weakest link is producer width at 1 CTA/SM, which looks like the BULK=0 layout of full-cuda-onelaunch-warpspec-bulk-gather (1.77 TB/s). Before dispatch, add DIAGNOSIS's gather-only roofline DIAG and its 2-CTA/SM per-warpgroup-ring variant as in-run variants, fix the TILE=128 smem arithmetic, and move the gate to LESSONS' two-round rule.
justification: Mechanism: plausible. The profile backs every number. Full verify_16 is 162.5 us (FA3 148.7 + combine 6.4 + prepare 3.1 + norm-gate + pre-attn) against a 63.4 us floor. Verify_32 is 302.0 us (FA3 288.7) against 126.8 us. Master's CUDA stream-K decode kernel moves the same 256 B/token gather at 3.0-3.07 TB/s (decode_16 108.2 us), so decode-level bandwidth on verify (about 110/225 us) is a demonstrated ceiling, not a guess. s5 is correct (19 bisect cases, two-state replays). Its 0.570x/0.704x with 1.49x time for 2x bytes says it is latency-bound in a serial per-tile chain. Fixing that chain (S(n+1) issued before softmax(n), wait_group 1) is the right target. The compute fits (about 21 us of FP8 wgmma, about 40 us of MUFU at B=16) if it overlaps with a 108 us gather. q_len 8 x G 8 = 64 rows per kv head maps exactly onto m64 wgmma, one consumer warpgroup per kv head. The register budget fits (232x256 + 40x128 = 64,512). Expected shapes and directions match TASK: only full verify_16/32 move, decode, sliding and full verify_1 stay flat, and the milestones (M2 <=135/<=255 us, M3 <=95/<=190 us) sit between the incumbent and 1.5x floor. Weakest link: producer issue width and TLP at 1 CTA/SM. s5 ran 2 CTAs/SM with 512 issuing threads per SM, and master decode also has about 512 threads per SM in flight. This design has 128 issuers and 8 consumer warps per SM. That is the shape of full-cuda-onelaunch-warpspec-bulk-gather (1 CTA/SM, 8-stage ring, warp-specialized producer), whose BULK=0 per-thread 16 B cp.async variant capped at 1.77 TB/s with one producer warp. 4 producer warps instead of 1 is a real difference: 7 x 16 KB in flight easily covers Little's law at 3 TB/s, and about 32 warp-instructions per tile is little issue pressure. But nothing has yet shown that 4 warps reach 3 TB/s on a random 128 B row gather with a dependent page-index load per row. If they do not, M1 fails for a reason the consumer-side PHASE DIAG may only show indirectly (as long FULL waits). Prior: the frontmatter has no `prior` field. This is not grounds for hold: the body names s5 and the full_ws lesson, and DIAGNOSIS names s5 as the prior. The mechanism is different from s5 (overlapped, warp-specialized pipeline versus a serial chain with a CTA-wide EMPTY rendezvous). It is different from the do-not-try onelaunch item (a 128-thread cp.async producer warpgroup, not single-warp cp.async.bulk per row). It is different from the mma.sync verify do-not-try (wgmma). The churn tooling should add `prior: full-verify-wgmma-s5-qfrag-reload`. Concrete defect: 'Ring STAGES = 8 (8 x 16 KB = 128 KB)' is a 64-token tile (K 8 KB + V 8 KB for both heads). A TILE=128 stage is 32 KB, so 8 stages need 256 KB, more than the 227 KB per CTA. The TILE=128 variant must say STAGES=4-5 (or count stages in 64-token half-tiles). Otherwise it fails to launch or the builder improvises. The local-bytes>0 refusal does not catch an smem overflow, so the variant also needs an smem-size refusal. The DIAGNOSIS additions are not in the change text: (a) a gather-only roofline DIAG (same ring and producer, no MMA) and (b) a 2-CTA/SM variant that keeps s5's all-threads-issue layout, splits the ring per warpgroup and overlaps S(n+1). Add both as template variants in the same module. They answer the weakest link inside this one run.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup / paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: these define the incumbent (paired FA3 + prepare + combine + _paired_norm_gate_kernel at full verify B>1). They do not confound the measured kernel, but the prepare gate must time exactly master's paired path, including the paired pre-attention q layout and the norm-gate, or the >=1.05x routing decision is mis-anchored. When the wgmma path routes, the pre-attention kernel's q layout must be the one the wgmma kernel expects, not the paired-padded layout.

fused-preattention-triton: the wgmma path keeps _pre_attention_kernel as its prologue. If the routed band changes the PAIRED constexpr passed to it, verify_16/32 pre-attention time (2.7/4.1 us) can move a few us either way and be misread as kernel gain or loss. Read the replaced kernels' own top_kernels, not the shape total.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv / full-decode-splitkv-s2 stream-K (master decode kernel): it shares the load_inline import clock (222 s across 4 modules) and its ticket arrays. A new module adds compile time and a self-check, but there is no timing interaction on decode shapes, because they are untouched and gated by config.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite, judged on the replaced kernels' own us at verify_16/32 against 162.5/302.0 and the floor, and the hard prepare gate makes the decision fail-safe (no route means master is re-measured). No landed hypothesis is a plausible cause of a move on those rows except through the incumbent definition, and the gate already times that path. The real single-run ambiguity is why it fails to route: producer issue width at 1 CTA/SM, or consumer latency at 1 CTA/SM. Separate checks are the wrong fix. Resolve it inside the run by building (a) DIAGNOSIS's gather-only roofline instantiation (producer plus ring, consumers just wait FULL and arrive EMPTY; time it at B=16 x 80K and print achieved TB/s) and (b) the 2-CTA/SM per-warpgroup-ring overlapped variant, as extra template instantiations in the same muse_full_verify_wgmma_ws_v1 module. Both are timed in the same interleaved harness, and either may route. The extra compile cost is one module. The next stage is the follow-up.
rules_flags: Gate rule mismatch: the change routes on one median-of-40 >= 1.05x. LESSONS (2026-10-25) now requires two interleaved rounds, both >= 1.03, with candidate IQR <= 1.5x master's. Use two rounds, each >= 1.05, plus the IQR bound, so a noisy route cannot ship a loser. This is a correctness-of-routing issue, not a competition rule.

Two-state rotation: the ticket and partial-slot arrays and any page-index prefetch buffer must be shape/config-sized and self-resetting. No static may hold a state's device pointer. The change text says so. The audit should verify it for the new producer's page-index smem ring and any global scratch.

Every key: stream-K tile boundaries and partial-segment masking must attend every context key, including the last partial tile and the 8 new verify tokens with their causal mask. Rely on s5's bisect table, which must be run per routed variant, including the TILE=128 and 2-CTA/SM variants.

Precision: P is FP8 with Max_offset 8 (as in s5) and Q is FP8 E4M3, both within the rules (q at most FP8, fp32 softmax and merges). Keep the rel-L2 < 3e-2 cross-check against master at 80K in the gate.

setmaxnreg / launch_bounds(384,1): no rules issue, but check that kernel_fn takes no host-side occupancy query or cudaFuncSetAttribute per call. Set the max-dynamic-smem attribute once at import/prepare.
open_questions: TILE=128: what is STAGES? 8 x 32 KB does not fit in 227 KB. Specify 4 (or 5 with no other large smem) and add a refusal when dynamic smem exceeds the device limit, alongside local bytes > 0.

Does the 128-thread producer warpgroup sustain >= 2.8 TB/s on its own? The gather-only DIAG (DIAGNOSIS 1a) should answer this before the consumers are blamed. The BULK=0 single-warp precedent was 1.77 TB/s.

Page-index prefetch: how far ahead does the producer load page indices relative to the K/V issue? A dependent int32 load per row on the producer's critical path can cap issue rate more than the width can.

cp.async.mbarrier.arrive.noinc with 128 producer arrivals per FULL stage, plus EMPTY with 256 consumer arrivals: are expected counts initialised once and phase bits tracked per stage across stream-K segment boundaries (s4/s5's bug class was per-segment state)?
With two S accumulator sets at TILE=128 (2 x 64 regs) plus O (32) plus softmax temps, does the consumer stay under 232 regs with no spill? Print it per variant, as specified.
Should the gate also offer the 2-CTA/SM per-warpgroup-ring variant (DIAGNOSIS 1b), so that a 1-CTA/SM TLP loss does not leave the stage with nothing routed?
